newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong newspapers report Deng's health worsens.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong newspapers report Deng's health worsens.

text.p: China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was sent to hospital recently after his health deteriorated, Hong Kong newspapers reported on Tuesday.
The reports could not immediately be independently confirmed in Beijing.

The independent Sing Tao Daily quoted an informed Beijing source as saying the 92-year-old patriarch and architect of China's economic reforms was sent to the Number 301 military hospital in Beijing's western suburbs last week.
In a separate report, Hong Kong's Apple Daily, quoting Taiwan cable television, said Deng's health had worsened suddenly and he had been sent to hospital in a critical state.
Last week, however, Beijing's vice-mayor Zhang Baifa said Deng was in good health, but that he might not be able to visit Hong Kong when the British colony reverts to China next July 1.
"To my knowledge (Deng's health) is very good," Zhang told reporters on December 23 when asked at a reception for diplomats and journalists.
But he added: "It would be difficult for him to (go to Hong Kong) now. It would be disastrous for an old man in his 90s to catch cold. Catching cold would be a serious illness."
This week China's Central television station is launching a 12-part documentary on Deng's life and times.
